numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Writing int64 data to a compressed FITS image with CompImageHDU (quantize_method=1, RICE_1 / HCOMPRESS path) produces a corrupted compressed file because of an upstream bug; the BYTEPIX header value is not set correctly (should be 8 for int64 data).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Creating compressed files with (u)int64 data should be prevented: data is converted to (u)int32 if possible without overflow, otherwise an error is raised. For HCOMPRESS with 64-bit ints, the path should be disabled, while GZIP algorithms should keep working.

HCOMPRESS compression applied to 64-bit integer data

numerical_characteristics.dtype: (u)int64 integer data written with CompImageHDU compression (RICE_1, PLIO_1 and HCOMPRESS-related paths)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: values that would overflow 32-bit integer range when compressed; overflow case adds np.iinfo(np.int32).max to the data
category_specific_evidence: Issue #19577 reproducer packs a PrimaryHDU of int data (np.random.poisson(1000)) with quantize_method=1 and quantize_level 64 or 1e9 and writes test-fpack.fits.fz, then runs funpack.
PR discussion: HCOMPRESS only supports 32-bit; the '64' function avoids overflow for 32-bit ints, but 64-bit ints would risk overflow without a '128' function.
Commit: prevent creating compressed files with (u)int64 data; if possible without overflow data is converted to (u)int32, otherwise an error is raised.
Changelog 19592.bugfix: prevent creating RICE_1 or PLIO_1 compressed files with (u)int64 data; convert to (u)int32 if possible without overflow, otherwise raise an error.

Added test test_decompress_integers parametrized over nbytes (2, 4, 8) and overflow (False/True); for RICE_1/PLIO_1 with 8-byte data it expects a ValueError on overflow and an AstropyUserWarning otherwise, matching '<COMPRESSION_TYPE> compression doesn't support 64 integers'.
Passages do not mention NaN, infinity, signed zero or subnormal handling; special floating-point values are not addressed.
reproduction_risks: Silent int64 to int32 conversion may lose data if values exceed int32 range; the passages state conversion happens only when it is possible without overflow.
The reproducer in issue #19577 is incomplete for special values: it uses only integer Poisson data and no NaN/inf/signed-zero/subnormal cases.
Behaviour of HCOMPRESS with 64-bit data is unresolved in the discussion; the passages do not confirm the final behaviour for it.
